bull.b: Sustained high gross margins (~57%–60%) and strong operating profitability (Q2 operating margin ~33.7%) indicate durable unit economics and pricing power in ATE and automation. These margins support reinvestment in R&D, absorb cyclical revenue swings, and underpin long-term cash generation.

bull.t: Conservative balance sheet and strong ROE
bull.b: Very low leverage and attractive ROE reflect capital-efficient operations and financial flexibility. A conservative balance sheet reduces refinancing risk through semiconductor cycles and allows opportunistic buybacks, dividends and targeted CapEx without jeopardizing liquidity over the medium term.

bull.t: AI-driven TAM expansion and share opportunity
bull.b: A >60% revenue mix from AI workloads and management's view of a multi-year ATE TAM expansion provide structural demand tailwinds. Strong exposure to compute, HBM/DRAM and hyperscaler programs supports sustained order flow and positions the company to convert platform leadership into lasting share gains.

bear.b: Cash conversion has been inconsistent, with operating cash flow under net income in multiple years and volatile free-cash-flow growth. In cyclic end markets, uneven cash conversion can stress funding for working capital, slow buyback pacing, and make capital allocation timing more difficult over the medium term.

Management disclosed inventory increases to support ramps, which ties up cash and raises execution risk if customer qualification or order timing slips. Elevated inventory can compress near-term FCF and requires reliable demand visibility to avoid margin-dilutive write-downs during industry slowdowns.

bear.t: Memory & product-mix margin pressure and timing uncertainty
bear.b: Memory-driven margin headwinds and product-mix shifts can limit margin expansion even amid strong revenue. Additionally, long qualification and ramp timelines (9–12 months) create execution risk for converting design wins into revenue, delaying expected share gains and cash benefits over the medium term.
